bugs.title: SiteConfig/Profile tenantId index defined twice, model init fails
bugs.description: Creating indexes for SiteConfig and Profile threw 'An existing index has the same name as the requested index', so the app could not start against a fresh database.
bugs.repro: Run the plugin unit tests on an empty database; the suite failed in Model.init().
bugs.rootCause: tenantScoped plugin adds tenantId with index:true and the singleton models also declared a unique { tenantId: 1 } index; both get the auto name tenantId_1
bugs.fix: tenantScoped(schema, { index: false }) for singleton models; SiteConfig and Profile use it

bugs.title: Tenant context lost when a lazy Mongoose Query is returned from the tenant runner
bugs.description: runInTenant(A, () => Post.find()) threw 'no tenant context' because the query ran after the context ended. Any job or script written the same way would fail, and a future 'fix' might be tempted to loosen the fail-closed check.
bugs.repro: Call runInTenant with a callback that returns a Query without awaiting it.
bugs.rootCause: runInTenant returned the un-awaited Query. Mongoose queries execute on await, after AsyncLocalStorage.run() has exited, so the tenant plugin saw no context. The plugin correctly failed closed (no data leaked); the helper was the defect.
bugs.fix: runInTenant/runWithCtx are async and await the callback inside the context; documented in docs/05

bugs.title: Soft-delete aggregate filter appended after $group, deleted rows still counted
bugs.description: Aggregations (dashboard counts, statistics) included soft-deleted documents. Wrong numbers with no error message, so nobody would notice.
bugs.repro: Soft-delete one of two posts, then aggregate with a $group count: returns 2 instead of 1.
bugs.rootCause: The aggregate hook used pipeline.push, so the isDeleted filter ran after earlier stages such as $group instead of before them.
bugs.fix: aggregate hook now unshifts the $match so it runs first

bugs.title: PATCH /posts/:id demanded a title on every partial update
bugs.description: Editing only the summary (or any single field) of a post returned 400 VALIDATION_FAILED. The admin form would not be able to autosave partial changes.
bugs.repro: PATCH /admin/tenants/:id/posts/:postId with body { summary: '...' } and no title.
bugs.rootCause: update() reused the create/draft schema where title is required, so a partial body such as { summary } failed validation with 400.
bugs.fix: new postPatchSchema (all fields optional, title min 3 if present) used by PostService.update

bugs.title: Tenant SMS cap overrode the platform cap, so the SMS cost limit did nothing
bugs.description: A bot flooding the complaint form could send up to the tenant limit (500/day) regardless of the platform cap, so an SMS cost-exhaustion attack (MIS-03) was not contained by the platform-level control.
bugs.repro: Set DAILY_SMS_CAP=3, submit 6 complaints: all 6 acknowledgement SMS were sent.
bugs.rootCause: SmsService used p.cap ?? defaultCap; the caller always passed the tenant setting (default 500), so the platform-wide DAILY_SMS_CAP was never applied.
bugs.fix: effective cap = min(tenant cap, platform cap)

bugs.title: Unverified custom domain served the MP's site
bugs.description: Anyone who pointed a domain at the platform after a super admin registered it (or before the owner proved control) would get the MP's public site served under their own address, enabling impersonation or phishing with real MP content.
bugs.repro: Add a custom domain via POST /super/tenants/:id/domains; GET /public/site with that Host returns 200 without any DNS verification.
bugs.rootCause: resolveHost looked up the Domain row only; dnsStatus was never checked, so a custom domain was served as soon as it was added.
bugs.fix: resolveHost returns 404 for a custom domain until dnsStatus is active (verified TXT)

bugs.title: RATE_LIMIT_DISABLED=false still disabled rate limiting
bugs.description: An operator who writes RATE_LIMIT_DISABLED=false (to be explicit) would silently switch OFF all rate limits, leaving login, OTP and complaint endpoints open to brute force and SMS-cost abuse, with no error or log line.
bugs.repro: loadConfig({ ...valid, RATE_LIMIT_DISABLED: 'false' }).RATE_LIMIT_DISABLED === true
bugs.rootCause: z.coerce.boolean() converts any non-empty string, including 'false', to true.
bugs.fix: flag parsed with an explicit enum (true/false/1/0) and unknown values are rejected at boot

bugs.title: Valid Wikimedia image URLs with Bangla file names were rejected (500 char limit)
bugs.description: Posts and banners using real licensed photos with Bangla file names failed validation, so the seed (and real editors) could not attach them.
bugs.repro: Create a post with the hero image URL from client-demo data.js.
bugs.rootCause: media and banner url max(500); percent-encoding expands each Bangla character to 9 characters, so realistic URLs are longer.
bugs.fix: url limit raised to 1500 in mediaRefSchema and siteConfigSchema

bugs.title: Auth rate limit was per IP (10 per 15 min): offices and mobile-carrier users get locked out
bugs.description: The officer's login failed with 429 during the end-to-end run. In production, staff on a shared IP could not sign in, while the 2FA endpoints had no per-account limit at all.
bugs.repro: Log in 4 different staff accounts from one IP within 15 minutes.
bugs.rootCause: The auth tier limited 10 requests per 15 minutes per IP, and each login is 3 requests (password, enrol, code). Three colleagues behind one office or CGNAT address exhausted it, while brute-force protection should be keyed to the account.
bugs.fix: IP tier raised to 60/15min; new per-account tier (10/15min) on login and on the MFA endpoints keyed by the verified mfa-token subject

bugs.title: Opening a second complaint navigated to a nested broken URL and bounced to the home page
bugs.description: In the officer/owner inbox the first click worked but every following click on another complaint left the inbox, so complaints could effectively be handled one per page load.
bugs.repro: Open the inbox, click a complaint, then click a different one.
bugs.rootCause: nav(c.id) is route-relative; from complaints/:cid it appended the new id to the current path (/complaints/<id1>/<id2>), which matches no route and fell through to the catch-all redirect.
bugs.fix: single splat route complaints/* and absolute navigation to /t/<tenant>/complaints/<id>

bugs.title: Dashboard API sent complaint statistics to editors (and content data to officers)
bugs.description: The PR editor's dashboard showed open-complaint counts and SLA although the role matrix gives editors no access to complaints. Aggregates only (no identities), but it breaks least privilege and the documented role table.
bugs.repro: Log in as editor, open the dashboard: complaint cards are present.
bugs.rootCause: GET /dashboard returned the whole aggregate for any role holding dashboard.view; only officers were trimmed. The PR editor has no complaint permissions, but received the numbers, and the UI only hid nothing.
bugs.fix: dashboard response is built per permission (content vs complaint sections); UI hides cards the role cannot use

bugs.title: Time of day: 3:30 pm was shown as দুপুর instead of বিকেল
bugs.description: Timestamps in the audit log and complaint history used the wrong Bangla word for the hour between 3 and 4 pm.
bugs.rootCause: day-part thresholds used 16:00 as the start of বিকেল; Bangla convention starts it at 15:00.
bugs.fix: thresholds corrected and ভোর added (4-5)

bugs.title: Save draft with only a title failed: empty form fields were sent as empty strings
bugs.description: PR staff could not save a quick draft: the form showed confusing errors for fields they had not touched.
bugs.repro: Open New post, type only a title, press Save draft.
bugs.rootCause: The editor sent every field, including untouched ones as '', and the shared schema rejects summary '' (min 10). The documented rule 'a draft needs only a title' could not be used from the UI.
bugs.fix: empty fields are omitted from the payload (body/quote/upazila/place stay clearable when editing)

bugs.title: E2E: officer login stuck once after fresh dev-server start (not reproduced in 3 later runs)
bugs.description: During the first e2e run right after the dev servers started, the officer's TOTP enrolment did not reach the dashboard within 15 s. Later runs (and an isolated debug run) passed. Suspects: cold tsx/vite start, TOTP step boundary, dev rate limit. e2e/smoke.py now prints the URL, network errors and alerts when a login gets stuck.
bugs.repro: Start dev:api and dev:admin, immediately run bash e2e/run.sh

bugs.title: Form inputs without a type attribute were unstyled (about 21 px high, no padding): the CSS only matched typed inputs
bugs.description: base.css styled input[type=text] etc., but almost every input in the SPA has no type attribute, so titles, place, credit fields rendered as thin default browser boxes. Reported by the owner from a screenshot.
bugs.repro: Open Posts > New post; measure the title input height
bugs.rootCause: CSS selectors listed input types explicitly and never the untyped default
bugs.fix: extra.css now styles input:not([type]) together with the typed selectors (min-height 52px, 16px font, padding); e2e/smoke.py asserts every composer text field is at least 48 px high

bugs.title: Public site API showed the seat number with an English digit (নদীপুর-3)
bugs.description: publicSite built the seat label from seatNumber without toBn, so every public page header would show নদীপুর-3.
bugs.repro: GET /api/v1/public/site with the demo host; mp.seat
bugs.rootCause: number interpolated directly into a Bangla string
bugs.fix: toBn(seatNumber) in services/site.ts publicSite; regression assertion in content.test.ts

bugs.title: Public site: sanitiser produced mismatched closing tags after an unsafe link in a post body
bugs.description: sanitize-html transformTags renamed an unsafe to ; the closing tag of the NEXT safe link was then emitted as , giving malformed HTML (ok). Browsers repair it, but link text could swallow following content.
bugs.repro:
sanitizeBody('

bad ok

')
bugs.rootCause: sanitize-html closes function-renamed tags inconsistently
bugs.fix: unsafe links keep the <a> tag name with no attributes (inert); regression test in apps/web-public/test/helpers.test.ts

bugs.title: Super Admin audit API returned the citizen's IP address and browser user agent for public complaint submissions (and officers' free-text reasons for identity views)
bugs.description: GET /api/v1/super/audit returned raw AuditLog rows. audit() stores the request IP and user agent from the request context; for complaint.create written by the public complaint endpoint that is the complainant's IP and UA, and complaint.pii_view rows carry the officer's free-text purpose. Super admin and support must never see complainant identity (ADR-0004, docs/08).
bugs.repro: Submit a complaint on the public site, then GET /api/v1/super/audit as super admin or support: the complaint.create row has ip and userAgent.
bugs.rootCause: The route returned raw AuditLog documents (.lean()) and audit() records the request IP/UA even for unauthenticated public submissions.
bugs.fix: GET /super/audit now maps rows through auditForStaff(): user agent never sent; complaint.* rows lose ip and reason; ip only for authenticated admin actions and only to super_admin (support never); tenant names joined. Regression test in apps/api/test/integration/super-dashboard.test.ts.

bugs.title: Tenant audit API returns the complainant's IP address and user agent to the owner (complaint.create rows)
bugs.description: GET /api/v1/admin/tenants/:id/audit (audit.view: owner, act-as super admin, support) returns raw AuditLog rows including ip and userAgent. complaint.create rows are written by the public complaint endpoint, so ip/userAgent are the citizen's. Owners and platform staff never have complaints.pii_view. Root-cause options: audit() should not store ip/UA when there is no authenticated actor, and/or the tenant route should project them out like auditForStaff() in routes/super.ts. Not fixed by the Super Admin agent (admin.ts / lib/audit.ts are outside its lane).
bugs.repro: Submit a complaint on the public site; GET /admin/tenants/:id/audit as the owner: the complaint.create row carries ip and userAgent.
bugs.rootCause: audit() copied request IP/UA for every action including public submissions, and the tenant audit route returned raw rows
bugs.fix: lib/audit.ts no longer stores IP/user agent for unauthenticated (citizen) actions; tenant GET /audit selects out ip/userAgent and drops reasons on complaint.* rows; regression test in complaints.test.ts (mutation-checked)

bugs.title: API: public per-IP rate limit (120/min) throttles the whole server-rendered public site; media files share the same bucket
bugs.description: routes/public.ts applies limit('public', byIp) to every public read and to /media files. The Next.js public site renders on the server, so every visitor's page view becomes ~6-10 API calls from the site server. Unless every hop forwards X-Forwarded-For correctly (trust proxy = 1 hop only), all visitors share one 120/min bucket; even per visitor, ~12 page views/min (plus every uploaded image/video file request) trips it and pages turn into 500s. Seen in the public-site smoke test: pages failed with RATE_LIMITED after ~15 page loads. The site now caches reads for 5 s and forwards the visitor IP, which reduces but does not remove the risk.
bugs.repro: Load 15 pages of the public site within a minute from one IP (python apps/web-public/e2e/public_smoke.py) -> GET /api/v1/public/* returns 429, site shows the error page. Suggested fix: separate (much higher) limit or a signed server-to-server key for the site renderer, and a separate limiter for /media files.
bugs.fix: API: X-Site-Token + X-Client-IP trusted only with the shared secret, separate media tier (lead). Site: server reads and the complaint/OTP/tracking proxy send x-site-token + x-client-ip (server-only env SITE_SERVER_TOKEN, X-Forwarded-For fallback without a token, incoming values never forwarded), 5 s read cache with stale-on-429/5xx; tests in apps/web-public/test/helpers.test.ts + apps/api/test/integration/site-server.test.ts

bugs.title: Saving the profile from the old Site page wiped portrait, milestones, education and every other profile field (PUT /profile replaced the whole draft with 3 fields)
bugs.description: The legacy ProfileCard on the Site page sent only {headline, intro, story} to PUT /profile. The alias forwards to PageService.put, which parses with defaults and replaces the draft, so portrait, milestones, committees, education, profession, politics, awards, works, parliament and priorities were silently emptied; the owner's next publish would put a gutted biography of the MP on the public site.
bugs.repro: Open Site page as owner, edit the profile headline, save: GET /pages/profile shows empty milestones/portrait.
bugs.rootCause: The legacy alias forwarded a partial body to a replace-the-whole-draft service, and the old card only sent three fields.
bugs.fix: PUT /profile now merges the partial body onto the current draft; the Site page no longer has a profile card (profile has its own full editor at site-pages/profile). Regression: apps/api/test/integration/pages.test.ts + web-admin content.test.tsx (BUG-2026-021).

bugs.title: Tabs variant=pill draws a stray status-pill dot before the tab list (class 'tabs pill' also matches .pill::before)
bugs.description: Tabs with variant pill render class 'tabs pill'; the status pill rule .pill::before adds a 6px dot left of the tabs.
bugs.repro: Open /media or /events: a dot appears before the tab group.
bugs.rootCause: Variant class name 'pill' collides with the status-pill class.
bugs.fix: content.css: .tabs.pill::before{content:none}; regression in src/styles.test.ts. The design-system owner may move the rule into ds.css or rename the variant class.

bugs.title: Public site: server-side API calls lost the tenant Host header (Node fetch overrides Host), production tenant resolution would fail
bugs.description: Node's global fetch (undici) replaces a custom Host header with the URL host. The API resolves the tenant by Host in production (X-Forwarded-Host is honoured only outside production), so every public page would 404 in production while working in development.
bugs.repro: fetch('http://127.0.0.1:4000/...', {headers:{host:'ndp3.jonoprotinidhi.com'}}) -> API sees host 127.0.0.1:4000
bugs.rootCause: undici fetch treats Host as a forbidden/overridden header
bugs.fix: server-to-API calls use node:http(s) (src/lib/http.ts) which keeps the Host header; regression test in apps/web-public/test/helpers.test.ts

bugs.title: Banners page lost edits typed in quick succession (state updates built from a stale copy of the form)
bugs.description: setF({...f, ...}) used the form object captured at render time; two edits before a re-render (autofill, fast typing, a finished upload plus an edit) overwrote each other, so a new banner was saved without its title and caption.
bugs.repro: e2e/cms_smoke.py banner step: fill title and caption right after adding a banner, save: title missing on GET /public/site.
bugs.rootCause: State built from the render-time copy of the form.
bugs.fix: Site.tsx updates the form only through functional state updates (up(fn)); regression test in content.test.tsx.

bugs.title: Photo picker's 'earlier uploads' library also listed uploaded videos (a .webm could be chosen as an image)
bugs.description: GET /media without kind returned images and videos; videos showed as broken images and could be set as a post/portrait/banner photo.
bugs.repro: Upload a video, open any photo picker, click 'আগে আপলোড করা ছবি থেকে'.
bugs.rootCause: The media library gained videos; the picker's query predates that.
bugs.fix: ImagePicker library requests /media?kind=image; regression in components/media.test.tsx.

bugs.title: Team invite with a password overwrote an existing platform user's password and status (account takeover)
bugs.description: TeamService.invite(): when the phone already belonged to a User (a member of any tenant, e.g. another MP's officer), an invite that carried a password ran User.updateOne({passwordHash, status: 'active'}) on that platform-wide account, and did so before the ALREADY_MEMBER check. Any tenant owner could set the password of any account whose phone number they knew, then log in as that person (cross-tenant).
bugs.repro: Owner of tenant B: POST /team/invites {phone: <tenant A editor's phone>, role: editor, password: 'X...'} -> the A editor's password is now X; even a 409 ALREADY_MEMBER attempt on tenant A changed the password first.
bugs.rootCause: invite() hashed and wrote the password onto whatever User owned the phone, and checked membership only afterwards
bugs.fix: services/team.ts invite(): membership conflict (409 ALREADY_MEMBER) and existing-account-with-password (409 ACCOUNT_EXISTS, Bangla: invite without a password) are decided before any write; an existing User's password/status is never touched; the password is hashed and set only when the User is created; audit after-diff carries passwordSetAtCreation: true (no hash).

bugs.title: Stored XSS: complaint attachments and voice notes were stored as arbitrary strings and rendered raw into iframe/a/img src in the admin
bugs.description: complaintSubmitSchema only length-checked files[].data and voiceNote.audioData. An anonymous citizen could submit data like 'javascript:...' or 'data:text/html,
bugs.repro: POST /api/v1/public/complaints with files: [{name: 'a.pdf', mimeType: 'application/pdf', size: 10, data: 'data:text/html;base64,PHNjcmlwdD4uLi48L3NjcmlwdD4='}] -> 201; owner opens the complaint and clicks the file -> the HTML runs inside the admin.
bugs.rootCause: attachment data URLs were only length-checked and stored/rendered verbatim
bugs.fix: API lib/attachments.ts (called in ComplaintService.submit after spam/rate checks): data:<mime>;base64 required, mime must equal mimeType, decoded bytes checked (PDF %PDF-, audio webm/ogg/mp4/mpeg/wav magic bytes, images decoded by sharp via processImage(maxEdge 1600) -> WebP, EXIF dropped), stored data URL rebuilt from the bytes; shared schema checks the data URL shape. Admin (defence in depth) safeMedia.ts: only image/webp|jpeg|png, application/pdf, audio/* prefixes are decoded, always shown via Blob object URLs with a fixed type (img, iframe, audio, download).

bugs.title: Complaint with large attachments could exceed MongoDB's 16 MB document limit and fail with a 500
bugs.description: Up to 5 files of 5 MB (about 6.7 MB each as base64) plus a 4 MB voice note were accepted by the schema; the stored document could pass 16 MB, Complaint.create threw and the citizen got 'server problem' with the complaint lost. The public form did not downscale photos (phone photos are often 3-8 MB) or enforce any total, and its 3-minute voice limit disagreed with the server's 300 s.
bugs.repro: Submit 5 x 5 MB images + a voice note -> 500 INTERNAL.
bugs.rootCause: no total size limit; 5 x 5 MB files + 4 MB voice could pass 16 MB; the form sent full-size photos
bugs.fix: shared complaintLimits.ts + schema superRefine: files + voice <= 12 MB of base64 (Bangla field error on files), voice <= 180 s (= the form); API re-checks the total after re-encoding (422); ComplaintBox shrinks photos to 1600 px JPEG 0.8 before base64, enforces per-file, total and 4 MB voice caps with Bangla messages, records at 32 kbps, timer uses the shared 180 s.

bugs.title: Complaint inbox list and CSV export loaded every voice note and attachment (megabytes per row)
bugs.description: list() returned view(c) with the full voiceNote.audioData and files[].data for every row of the page, and exportCsv() loaded up to 20,000 full documents into memory although it writes no attachment column. One page of 15 complaints with attachments could be hundreds of MB; the export could exhaust the API's memory.
bugs.repro: Submit 15 complaints with a voice note and photos, open the admin inbox -> the list response contains every base64 payload.
bugs.rootCause: list/export used find() without projection and view() returned the payloads
bugs.fix: list() projects out voiceNote.audioData and files.data; view() returns only hasVoice, voiceSec, fileCount, fileMeta (patch responses too); get() alone adds voiceNote/files payloads; exportCsv selects only its eight columns. Admin list shows ভয়েস / Nটি ফাইল from the flags.

bugs.title: Voice-only complaint: empty description crashed the model (500), so the form stored a canned sentence as the citizen's own words
bugs.description: The schema allows description '' when a voice note is attached, but the Mongoose model had description required: true, so Complaint.create threw a ValidationError (mapped to 500). The public form hid this by replacing an empty description with 'ভয়েস রেকর্ডের মাধ্যমে অভিযোগের বিবরণ প্রদান করা হয়েছে।', which was then stored and shown to staff as text the citizen wrote. Mongoose ValidationErrors in general surfaced as 500 instead of 400.
bugs.repro: POST /api/v1/public/complaints with description '' and a voiceNote -> 500.
bugs.rootCause: model description required: true contradicted the schema; the form papered over it with canned text
bugs.fix: models/complaints.ts description default '' (not required); canned sentence removed from ComplaintBox; admin detail shows 'শুধু ভয়েস অভিযোগ (লিখিত বিবরণ নেই)' for an empty description; app.ts error handler maps mongoose ValidationError to 400 VALIDATION_FAILED (field names only).

bugs.title: 25 MB JSON body parser ran before auth and rate limits for any POST path ending in /complaints
bugs.description: app.ts used express.json({limit: '25mb'}) for every POST whose path ends with /complaints, globally and before authentication or any rate limiter (admin and unknown paths included), so anyone could make the API buffer and parse 25 MB bodies at will. The public-site proxy read the whole body (any size) into memory before checking a 25 MB cap that applied to every allowed POST, OTP calls included.
bugs.repro: POST /api/v1/admin/tenants/<any>/complaints with a 24 MB JSON body and no token -> the body is fully parsed before the 401.
bugs.rootCause: the 25 MB parser was chosen by path suffix globally, before routing, auth and rate limits; the proxy read bodies fully before checking a shared 25 MB cap
bugs.fix: app.ts keeps the 1 MB parser for everything except exactly POST /api/v1/public/complaints; that route parses with a 13 MB limit inside the public router, after host resolution, the public tier and a new pre-parse complaintBody tier (10/min per IP), then strips operators. Next proxy (lib/bodyLimit.ts): 13 MB for complaints, 16 KB for OTP, Content-Length checked before reading, size counted while reading; response cap back to 256 KB. Staff complaint route keeps 1 MB.

bugs.title: Retention job left voice notes and attachments in place after removing the complainant's identity
bugs.description: purgeExpiredPii() unset pii and phoneHmac only. A citizen's recorded voice (identifying) and photos/documents stayed in the record forever, and anonymous complaints were never touched at all.
bugs.repro: Close a complaint with a voice note, advance past retention, run purgeExpiredPii() -> voiceNote.audioData and files[] are still stored.
bugs.rootCause: retention only unset pii/phoneHmac and skipped anonymous complaints
bugs.fix: purgeExpiredPii() also unsets voiceNote and files with the identity, and a second scoped updateMany removes voice/files from any other expired complaint (anonymous or already purged); audited with counts.

bugs.title: Complaint status/note form: a note from an unassigned in-scope officer failed with 403
bugs.description: The new status form sent note-only submissions through PATCH /complaints/:id, which requires complaints.manage or being the assigned officer; an in-scope but unassigned officer (who may add notes) got 'এই অভিযোগ আপনাকে দেওয়া হয়নি'. The status selector was also shown to officers who are not allowed to change the status.
bugs.repro: Officer opens an unassigned complaint of their upazila, types a note in the status form, presses 'আপডেট করুন' -> 403.
bugs.rootCause: the form sent note-only edits through PATCH, which needs manage or assignment; the UI did not know who may change status
bugs.fix: API get() returns canUpdate (manage or assigned officer). Admin: status form (selector, assignment) and SMS buttons shown only when canUpdate; a note-only submit from the status form goes to POST /complaints/:id/notes; status change sends PATCH with the note.

bugs.title: Public complaint form showed developer text to citizens (http://localhost:3000, raw exception names)
bugs.description: On a non-secure origin the voice recorder told citizens to open http://localhost:3000, and other microphone failures printed the raw error name and message (e.g. 'NotReadableError: Could not start audio source').
bugs.repro: Open the complaint page over plain http on a LAN address and press the record button.
bugs.rootCause: debug-time messages left in citizen-facing copy
bugs.fix: ComplaintBox: secure-context message explains https:// and offers the written form; NotFound/no device and generic mic errors are friendly Bangla without exception names/messages.

bugs.title: API integration tests flake on macOS: supertest's wildcard listener can share a port with a local 127.0.0.1 app, which answers 404
bugs.description: supertest calls app.listen(0) on the wildcard address. On macOS a wildcard bind succeeds even when another local process (seen: a desktop app listening on 127.0.0.1:<ephemeral>) holds the same port on 127.0.0.1, and requests to 127.0.0.1 then reach that other process (text/plain 'Not found', no X-Request-Id/helmet headers). Setup steps in makeTenant/loginFlow fail with 'login/accept/mfa failed 404' in about 2 of 326 tests per full run, random files. Not related to product code.
bugs.repro: With another app listening on a 127.0.0.1 ephemeral port, run the API suite a few times: 1-2 random setup failures with a 404 whose headers are not Express's. Suggested fix: create the test server bound to 127.0.0.1 explicitly and pass the listening server to supertest.
bugs.rootCause: supertest listens on the wildcard address; macOS lets a 127.0.0.1-specific listener of another app share the port and win
bugs.fix: test/helpers/env.ts makeEnv(): the app is served by an http.Server bound to 127.0.0.1 (unref'd) and that server is passed to supertest; 3 consecutive full API runs green afterwards.
